key_insight: A physics-grounded welding digital twin combines thermal simulation and fast Gaussian-process predictions to screen robotic joining conditions before in-space testing.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help engineers select welding settings and evaluate control strategies for on-orbit assembly and repair before costly physical trials.
method: Finite-volume weld-pool model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates benchmarked using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis robot with proportional power-setting control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; 74/80 boundary-case responses fell within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative width band.
watch_item: Results remain simulation-based: gravity was assessed separately from the thermal equation, and thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation are still needed.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
